23171085.fingerprint: y_t = 128.9 on the kappa = 1/2 footing; every planet passes for y_t <= 7.7e5

23171085.test: Earth-Mars ranging residual: the cured kernel predicts a residual below 1e-14 m/s^2 at 1 AU for y_t >= 100, the uncured one predicts a0/2 = 4.7e-11 m/s^2 (1279x the bound); one year of ranging decides.

23397365.fingerprint: 340 ppm source-field boost vs |delta| below 1e-6 (model 1e-20); 30-50 ppm needed

23354043.test: Free central density in relaxed clusters (the record's own decisive prediction): the tethered component saturates at 214/258 Msun/pc^2, so any cluster core above that must be free component, measurable in a single resolved lensing or X-ray+kinematic fit.

23420675.anchor: truncated at the galaxy's own cosmic cold share

23482936.fingerprint: law holds to g_bar ~ 7e-14 m/s^2, amplitude 1.016 +- 0.086; spheroidals 1.45x above at 4.0 sigma; dwarfs +0.44 dex

This is the sharpest statement of the theory's central anomaly.
23482936.test: A kinematic selector that separates rotating from pressure-supported systems at fixed g_bar: five candidates already fail, so the test is a new one (e.g. velocity-dispersion-weighted shape) applied to the same isolated-lens sample.

23372002.fingerprint: original settling rule excluded at +68.7; condensed-only rule +2.03

23372002.test: The pre-declared primary run with gas expulsion (in progress at deposit time): if the condensed-only rule's +2.03 degrades past the frozen threshold under the pre-declared run, the shear pass is a post-hoc selection.

23396865.fingerprint: B = 1.064 [1.010, 1.122]; baryon-only CCBH conversion excluded at 7.8 sigma (s_b = 0.70) and 16.6 sigma (0.43); cold-dark conversion 0.9 sigma
23396865.delta: If black holes source dark energy, the converted mass cannot be baryons: 114 localised FRBs give B = 1.064 and exclude baryon-only conversion at 7.8-16.6 sigma, while converting the cold dark component is consistent at 0.9 sigma. 23396865.test: The FRB dispersion-measure amplitude at z > 1 with a larger localised sample: the deficit s_b = 0.70 is a 30% baryon removal, so a 200-FRB sample at the same host marginalisation either confirms B = 1 or finds the deficit.

23169118.fingerprint: a0 = 9.36e-11 m/s^2; kappa = 0.551 +- 0.043 measured, fitted not derived; a0^2(Q) = kappa^2 G (-K(Q))
23169118.delta: The programme's own identity is a0^2(Q) = kappa^2 G (-K(Q)): the MOND scale is the dark sector's PRESSURE, not its energy density. That is what makes a0(z) flat for w = -1, and it is the one place where the origin question is stated as an identification rather than a fit.
23169118.test: Measure w of the dark sector to the precision that separates -K(Q) from rho_DE: a0(z) inherits w, so a 1% a0(z) measurement at z ~ 2 (the pre-registered deep-MOND Tully-Fisher zero point) reads w to ~0.03.

23192441.fingerprint: kappa = 0.45 +- 0.07, 0.58 +- 0.18, 0.43 +- 0.08; 1/2 consistent; 2.1-2.2 sigma on the critical density
23192441.delta: The empirical basis for kappa is estimator-dependent: three SPARC estimators give 0.45 +- 0.07, 0.58 +- 0.18 and 0.43 +- 0.08, all consistent with 1/2 but 2.1-2.2 sigma from it on the critical density, and the coefficient is degenerate with H0 and the stellar M/L zero point. 23192441.test: A stellar M/L zero point measured independently (resolved stellar populations or a gas-dominated absolute scale): with it, the three estimators collapse to one and the 2.1-2.2 sigma becomes a real number.
